content.value_statement: Teams need clear architecture decisions before implementation. This skill guides requirement discovery and creates a Mermaid-based EventStorming design catalog.
actual_capabilities: Structures design work into five phases: requirements, big picture, processes, data and flows, and integration.
Prompts the assistant to ask clarifying questions before making architecture decisions.
Defines Mermaid templates for EventStorming, ER diagrams, state charts, and sequence diagrams.
Directs output into docs/design-catalog with a README navigation hub.
Sets boundaries to avoid implementation details such as SQL, deployment files, and code examples.
limitations: It produces design documentation, not application code or deployment configuration.
It depends on user answers for accurate requirements and constraints.
It does not verify Mermaid rendering or validate architecture choices automatically.
The scanned package includes only SKILL.md; referenced template files are not present.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Architecture
use_cases.description: Turn early requirements into a shared design catalog before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Align a Team on Domain Events
use_cases.description: Use EventStorming diagrams to discuss actors, commands, events, aggregates, and hotspots.

use_cases.title: Prepare Architecture Documentation
use_cases.description: Create Mermaid diagrams and a README that help stakeholders review a proposed system.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Design Catalog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new system design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a new appointment booking system. Ask me one requirements question at a time before creating diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Create EventStorming Diagrams
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after basic requirements are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an EventStorming big picture for a marketplace checkout flow. Include actors, commands, events, aggregates, external systems, and hotspots.

prompt_templates.title: Model Critical Processes
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed process modeling for important workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Detail the order fulfillment and refund processes. Keep the design conceptual and use Mermaid diagrams for process, state, and sequence views.

prompt_templates.title: Assemble a Complete Catalog
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complete architecture review package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a full design catalog for a multi-tenant SaaS billing platform. Include requirements, EventStorming, data relationships, state transitions, key flows, and README navigation.

output_examples.input: Design a subscription billing system for a small SaaS product.
output_examples.output: A requirements summary, EventStorming big-picture view, focused process diagrams, conceptual data model, state views, sequence flows, and README navigation.

output_examples.input: Refine an existing checkout concept before implementation.
output_examples.output: Clarifying questions, documented hotspots for unclear policies, and Mermaid artifacts organized in a design catalog.

output_examples.input: Help my team agree on domain boundaries for an order system.
output_examples.output: Event-driven diagrams that show actors, commands, events, aggregates, external systems, and review points for team discussion.

best_practices: Answer requirements questions with real constraints before asking for diagrams.
Review each phase before moving to the next design artifact.
Keep artifacts conceptual and mark uncertain choices as hotspots.
anti_patterns: Skipping questions and treating default technology choices as facts.
Requesting deployment files, database migrations, or application code from this skill.
Creating many diagrams for low-value flows instead of focusing on critical processes.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a structured system design catalog with requirements notes, Mermaid diagrams, and README navigation.

faq.question: Does it generate application code?
faq.answer: No. It stays at the design level and avoids SQL, deployments, configuration files, and code examples.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What diagram formats does it use?
faq.answer: It requires Mermaid for EventStorming, entity relationships, state charts, and sequence diagrams.

faq.question: Where are the artifacts stored?
faq.answer: The instructions place generated artifacts under docs/design-catalog in the current project.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when implementation has already started or when you need code instead of design documentation.
